bull.b: Rapid expansion in AI customer ARR and overall revenue indicates strong adoption of DigitalOcean’s AI-native cloud offering. If sustained, this growth can broaden the customer base, increase workload intensity, and create durable cross-selling opportunities across compute, inference, storage, and managed services.

High adjusted margins and substantial free cash flow provide internal funding for capacity expansion while reducing reliance on external capital. This combination supports investment in AI infrastructure, strengthens resilience through the growth cycle, and demonstrates that expansion is translating into meaningful operating cash generation.

Multi-product usage increases customer integration with the platform and creates more opportunities to expand spending as workloads grow. Broad adoption across AI and core cloud services can improve retention, deepen switching costs, and make revenue less dependent on any single product category.

bear.b: New infrastructure can weigh on profitability when depreciation and lease costs begin ahead of utilization. Until added capacity reaches targeted revenue levels, gross-margin pressure may limit earnings conversion and cash efficiency, making sustained margin performance dependent on execution and ramp speed.

Debt materially exceeding equity reduces financial flexibility and increases the importance of maintaining reliable cash generation. Leverage can constrain investment choices during periods of weaker demand or lower margins, while the history of volatile equity suggests the capital structure has previously faced meaningful strain.

If industry supply expands faster than demand, pricing for compute and inference could normalize or decline. Lower realized prices would pressure revenue per unit of capacity and could weaken margins, returns on new infrastructure, and the pace at which AI demand converts into durable earnings growth.
